assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong, controllable coupling between a superconducting artificial atom and a single microwave photon routine, and it underlies dispersive readout, two-qubit gates and bus architectures in essentially every superconducting quantum processor. The idea is original, the physics is clean, and the impact on both quantum optics and quantum computing is lasting. From my own field I judge the lasting consequences to be very large, while remaining aware of proximity to my own work.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal and the first strong-coupling experiments are well documented. Girvin and Blais supplied key theory, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the experiments. With a four-name credit list, one theorist (Blais or Girvin) must be left out, which is a real allocation problem. I choose Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Girvin as the most defensible trio, acknowledging that Blais's role is substantial.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of independent replication across many groups and platforms, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits has prepared the ground without covering cQED itself. Timing is good, though a close follow-on to 2025 may be seen as too concentrated on one subfield.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would view cQED as sufficiently distinct from the 2025 award.
Allocation of theory credit between Girvin and Blais, and overlap with the Devoret, Martinis and Clarke circuit lineage.
My own field and institutional proximity may bias my sense of its importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates and later quantum-simulation ideas gave concrete physical routes to quantum computing, and the experimental realisations with ions (Blatt) demonstrated gates, entanglement and algorithms. The work is foundational, original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators of the ion-trap gate; Blatt is among the leading experimental realisers, alongside groups such as Wineland's, whose recognition came in 2012 and is a possible overlap. The three-name configuration is plausible, but the experimental credit is shared across several groups.
assessment.maturity: Mature: 1995 proposal, thirty years of independent confirmation, and now commercial platforms. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for single quantum-system control and with other experimental groups.
Whether ultracold-atom simulation and ion computing should be treated as one compound discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator are a conceptual advance in condensed matter, with a clean theoretical prediction, prompt experimental verification in HgTe, and a large subsequent field. Importance, originality and clarity are all high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the decisive theorists for the Z2 classification; Molenkamp led the HgTe observation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, and Fu, Kane and Moore for three dimensions are outside the supplied credit, so the configuration risks an unfair omission.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than a decade of confirmation by ARPES, transport and materials discovery, and stable interpretation. Following the 2016 topological-phase prize, it is timely but could be seen as partly covered.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors (Zhang and others) may be judged essential.
Degree of overlap with the 2016 topological phases prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength concept, achieved accuracy and stability at the 10^-18 level and opened precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The invention is original and has had lasting metrological impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye achieved the leading demonstrations and comparisons; this pairing is clean. Contributions of Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 and others in 2012 may be considered adjacent.
assessment.maturity: Mature and stable, with independent confirmation by many national laboratories. The redefinition of the second is ongoing, so the case is strengthening.
uncertainties: Whether the redefinition of the second will further shift credit.
Overlap with the thorium nuclear clock candidate that also includes Jun Ye.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field of tunable correlated and superconducting phases; the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the 2018 experiments are original and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald and Bistritzer made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery. Cory Dean and others contributed to related moire work, so an omission problem is possible.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated but the field is still evolving, and the pairing mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled. It may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Credit for related moire platforms and hBN heterostructure work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 launched quantum cryptography and connected foundations of quantum mechanics to practical information security; the concepts are original and have inspired a large experimental field.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the BB84 originators and Ekert the entanglement-based protocol, giving a natural three-person configuration. Wiesner's earlier ideas and the experimental demonstrations by others are an attribution wrinkle.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually mature, though practical deployment is still limited and the experimental implementations are a separate set of contributors. Some of this area was touched by the 2022 prize on entangled photons.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward conception or implementation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light turned a quantum-optics concept into a working precision-measurement resource, now used in gravitational-wave detectors beyond the standard quantum limit. The impact is concrete and well demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the interferometer theory, Kimble the early squeezing experiments, and Schnabel the later GEO600 and LIGO-oriented work, though the allocation versus Slusher, Walls, Mavalvala and the LIGO collaborations is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the interferometry setting with repeated confirmation, and related to the 2017 LIGO prize. Timing is acceptable.
uncertainties: Many contributors (Slusher, Wu, Walls and others) are not in the trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the electroweak symmetry-breaking mechanism and is a landmark result of the field.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory; for experiments, the spokespeople and architects named here are plausible, but collective credit among thousands of physicists is difficult to allocate and prize rules constrain the choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent confirmation by two experiments and subsequent coupling measurements. Recognition is arguably overdue relative to the 2013 theory prize but outside my own expertise.
uncertainties: Fair attribution in a large collaboration.
Whether the committee would prefer to treat the discovery as already recognised through the 2013 prize.
